_notes: Fallacies the app records silently and provokes later (docs/context-and-definitions.md, section 5). side: 'logic' means the mind was bypassed; 'meaning' means the heart was. The author will add meaningful fallacies. cues are case-insensitive regular expressions over one sentence; chain is the sequence of questions asked, one per turn, once the person asks the app something.

fallacies.name: Double standard
fallacies.description: One rule for me, another for them. The main meaningful fallacy.
chain: What would it look like if we reversed the roles? What would you do in their situation?
And what are all the reasons that person wouldn't see it the way you do?
Having listed those, what, if anything, looks different about the original situation?

fallacies.name: Weaponised togetherness (the ledger)
fallacies.description: The relationship or a past gift produced as an instrument: after everything I have done.
chain: When it was given, what did you want it to be?
What would the relationship look like if neither side kept the score?
fallacies.source: Beyond Flat Land ch. 13; Four Rivers on milk turned to debt

fallacies.name: Reduction to one mechanism
fallacies.description: The whole person reduced to one mechanism: you're just doing X.
chain: What three words come to mind for them?
What was the last thing they did that did not fit those words?

fallacies.name: Kitchen-sinking
fallacies.description: Many grievances fused into one generalisation that is not a claim.
chain: Which one of those is the one that matters most today?
If only that one were fixed, what would be left?

fallacies.name: The freeze-out
fallacies.description: The wall goes up, the account is closed, the ground is salted.
chain: What would have to be true for the door to open again?
Who do you know who would keep a gate in that wall, and what would they do?

fallacies.name: The unilateral fact
fallacies.description: The decision announced as already made: I've already done it.
chain: Who else had a stake in that decision?
What would they say they lost by not being asked?

fallacies.name: The zoom-out that erases the complaint
fallacies.description: This proves the whole relationship was a mistake.
cues: \bwhat'?s the point of any of it\b
chain: What is the actual complaint underneath, in one sentence?
When did that one thing last go well?

fallacies.name: Charm at the wrong moment
fallacies.description: The charm turned on hard at the exact moment charm is an insult.
chain: What did the other person need at that moment?
What would it have cost to give them that instead?

fallacies.name: Overgeneralisation (absolutes)
fallacies.description: Always, never, everyone, nobody: a definition that divides by zero.
cues: \b(always|never|everyone|everybody|no ?one|nobody|everything|nothing|every (single )?time|all the time|not once|without exception|every ?one of them|none of them|all of them)\b
chain: When was a time it went differently?
Out of the last ten times, how many went that way?

fallacies.name: False dilemma
fallacies.description: Only two options offered when more exist.
chain: If both of those were off the table, what would be left?
Who do you know who would find a third way here, and what would they do?

fallacies.name: Catastrophising
fallacies.description: The worst case treated as the certain case.
chain: Out of ten, what number would you put on that happening?
What would you watch for that would tell you it is actually going that way, and when will you check?
fallacies.source: Alphas and Postpartum: the alarm, the criterion, the re-check time

fallacies.name: Slippery slope
fallacies.description: A chain of consequences asserted without the steps.
chain: What would have to happen between here and there?
Which of those steps is the least certain?

fallacies.name: Mind reading
fallacies.description: Knowing what another person thinks or intends without their saying so.
cues: \b(he|she|they) (think|thinks|believe|believes|want|wants|meant|is|are|was|were) (just )?(trying to|out to|making me|doing it to|doing this to)\b
chain: What did they actually say or do?
What are all the other reasons someone might do that?

fallacies.name: Fortune telling
fallacies.description: A future outcome asserted as known.
cues: \b(it|this|that|he|she|they)('s| is| are|'ll| will) (going to|gonna|bound to|definitely going to|never going to)\b
chain: Out of ten, what number would you put on that?
What is the earliest sign that it is going the other way?

fallacies.name: Should statements
fallacies.description: A rule applied as if it were a law of nature.
cues: \b(should('ve| have)|shouldn'?t have|ought to have|(was|were) supposed to|must (always|never)|mustn'?t ever)\b
chain: Whose rule is that?
What would happen if it were not followed this once?

fallacies.name: Sunk cost
fallacies.description: Continuing because of what has already been spent.
chain: If you were starting today, with nothing spent, what would you choose?
What is the cost from here forward, leaving the past out of it?

fallacies.name: Appeal to popularity
fallacies.description: True because many people say so.
chain: Who specifically?
What does the person who disagrees say?

fallacies.name: Appeal to authority
fallacies.description: True because someone with standing said so.
chain: What did they actually see that led them to that?
What would change their mind?

fallacies.name: Post hoc
fallacies.description: After this, therefore because of this.
chain: What else changed around the same time?
Has the second thing ever happened without the first?

fallacies.name: Personalisation
fallacies.description: Everything that happened is because of me.
chain: What part of that was within your control, and what part was not?
Who else had a hand in it?

fallacies.name: Emotional reasoning
fallacies.description: I feel it, so it is true.
chain: What is the feeling, and what is the evidence, kept separate?
When did the feeling last turn out to be wrong?

fallacies.name: Tu quoque (what about you)
fallacies.description: Answering a point by pointing at the other person's conduct.
cues: \b(look who'?s talking|you'?re one to talk|what about (you|when you|the time you)|pot calling the kettle)\b
chain: If someone else had said the same thing, what would you make of it?
Is the point true on its own, leaving aside who said it?

fallacies.name: Labeling (self)
fallacies.description: A single failure turned into an identity.
chain: What is the specific thing that happened, without the label?
What would you say to a friend who did the same thing?

fallacies.name: Loaded question
fallacies.description: A question that assumes what it asks.
chain: What is the assumption inside that question?
When was a time that assumption did not hold?

fallacies.name: Straw man
fallacies.description: Answering a weaker version of what was said.
chain: What would they say they meant?
What is the strongest version of their point?
